technical_and_design_decisions: Port the existing Spring XD module implementations into the s-c-s repository rather than redesigning their functional behavior.
Adapt module configuration, lifecycle, metadata, packaging, and stream binding conventions to the target s-c-s architecture.
Implement router and file, FTP, Redis, and GemFire modules as sink-capable components, and Rabbit as a source-capable component, matching the user stories.
Preserve existing Spring XD semantics and configuration names where practical; document any unavoidable property or behavior changes.
Use the target repository's existing Java, Spring, build, dependency-management, testing, and code-style conventions.
Update Hadoop-related dependencies and configuration to support the selected current HDP/PHD releases while retaining HDFS integration compatibility.
Use automated unit and integration tests with mocked or containerized external services where practical; avoid requiring production infrastructure for normal test execution.
Treat migration documentation as repository documentation covering the 1.2-to-1.3 changes, improvements, compatibility notes, and required user actions.
assumptions: The existing Spring XD source code for all six modules is available and can be inspected and reused.
The s-c-s repository already exists and provides a working build, module template, and conventions for source and sink components.
No fundamental redesign of the modules or new public protocol is required.
The requested HDP/PHD versions are not specified; one currently supported and mutually compatible version line will be selected based on the repository's dependency constraints.
The increment targets Java 17 or a compatible Java 17+ runtime, consistent with Spring Framework 6 requirements.
External systems such as FTP servers, Redis, RabbitMQ, GemFire, and HDFS can be simulated, mocked, or run in a developer test environment.
Acceptance criteria consist of successful builds, automated tests, representative end-to-end module behavior, and reviewed documentation.
Effort includes implementation, testing, debugging, local integration, and developer documentation, but excludes release management, production deployment, and long-term operational support.
The estimates represent one developer's direct effort in workdays and do not represent elapsed calendar duration.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the s-c-s repository structure, build conventions, module APIs, existing tests, Spring XD implementations, and compatibility constraints; map each user story to target components and acceptance checks.

Create or adapt module projects, dependency declarations, metadata, configuration properties, packaging, and registration so the migrated components can build and be discovered in the target repository.
Migrate the router module, adapt its message routing and sink binding behavior to s-c-s conventions, preserve relevant configuration, and add focused unit tests.
Migrate the file sink, including path and file-name handling, write behavior, configuration mapping, error handling, target binding integration, and automated tests.

Migrate the FTP sink, including connection and authentication properties, file transfer behavior, resource handling, retry or failure behavior already supported by the source module, and test coverage.
Adapt the Redis sink to the target repository's dependency and binding model, preserve serialization and connection configuration, and implement unit and representative integration tests.
Adapt the Rabbit source module, including inbound connection, queue or exchange configuration, message conversion, source binding, lifecycle handling, and automated tests.
Migrate the GemFire sink, resolve client and serialization dependencies, map configuration and connection behavior to the target framework, and add tests for representative writes and failures.

Select compatible HDP/PHD dependency versions, update build and runtime configuration, resolve Hadoop API or transitive dependency changes, validate HDFS operations, and add compatibility tests or verification procedures.
Run full builds and representative source-to-sink pipeline scenarios, validate configuration metadata and packaging, diagnose interoperability issues, and fix regressions across all migrated modules.
Create the 1.2-to-1.3 migration section, documenting improvements, changed defaults and configuration, backward incompatibilities, upgrade steps, and module-specific considerations.

activities.activity_name: Final code quality, packaging, and delivery preparation
activities.activity_description: Apply formatting and static checks, review dependency licenses and versions, update README or module documentation, verify clean reproducible builds, and prepare the completed increment for review and merge.
